name: OP285 / OP285GP / OP285GS / OP285GSZ
tagline: The laser-trimmed precision twin of the OP275, praised in Chinese upgrade guides for a sweet, resolving midrange.

lineage.note: Unconfirmed: inferred from the OP prefix and OP275/OP285 Butler family. ADI bought PMI in 1990.
Owns the Rev. C datasheet. Non-Z SOIC parts discontinued by PDN 17_0038 (2017).

part_numbers.note: Family; ADI product page live. SOIC-8 today; Rev. C still shows PDIP outline.
8-lead PDIP. Reportedly obsolete since April 2002 (broker page only).
Non-RoHS SOIC-8 and reels; discontinued by PDN 17_0038, replaced by OP285GSZ.
RoHS SOIC-8 and reels. Arrow lists GSZ and -REEL7; ADI lifecycle unconfirmed.

key_specs.value: ±22 V abs. max (supply or input unconfirmed)

reputation.summary: A long-time Chinese upgrade favourite, usually named with the OP275. CN guides credit it with a soft, tube-like midrange, intimate vocals and high resolution. Head-Fi posters like its resolving treble but say it needs care in the circuit. diyAudio suggests it as a budget alternative to the OPA627/OPA637. All opinion, not measurement.
typical_uses: Op-amp rolling in DIY and Chinese DACs and preamps
I/V and output stages; precision alternative to OP275
caveats: Praise comes from reprinted CN guides and forum anecdotes, not measurements.
Head-Fi posters say it needs careful decoupling and loading to sound its best.
DIP-8 OP285GP reportedly obsolete since about 2002; socket rolling today means SOIC on adapter, old stock or remarks.
Headline specs match the OP275; it is not 'faster' than the OP275.

counterfeit_notes: No ADI advisory found. Marketplace listings lumping OP285G/GS/GSZ/GSZ-REEL into one product suggest mixed or remarked stock. Fresh-looking DIP OP285GP parts are likely old stock or remarks. Buy OP285GSZ from authorized distributors such as Arrow.
alternatives: OP275 (same front end, 1 mV offset grade)

silicon_changes.summary: ADI discontinued the non-RoHS OP285GS variants and named the pin-compatible OP285GSZ as replacement. No die change is documented; this is a part-number and lead-finish transition.
silicon_changes.identification: Non-Z SOIC part numbers are discontinued; the replacement carries the Z suffix (OP285GSZ, -REEL, -REEL7).
silicon_changes.audio_impact: None expected; no electrical or die change documented.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: pin-compatible Z-suffix replacement named in the PDN.
silicon_changes.verification: PDN revisions -, B and C located on ADI, Mouser and DigiKey.

open_questions: Print date of Rev. C, and dates and contents of Rev. 0, A and B.
Does the OP285 share the OP275 die (trim/test selection), or is it a separate die?
Current ADI lifecycle of OP285GSZ and reels; did an OP285GPZ (RoHS PDIP) ever exist?

claims_confirmed: Current ADI datasheet is 'Dual 9 MHz Precision Operational Amplifier OP285 Rev. C' (https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/op285.pdf).
250 µV offset, 6 nV/√Hz, 0.0006% THD, 22 V/µs, 9 MHz, 5 mA, 2 nA offset current (https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/op285.pdf).
Butler front end combines bipolar accuracy and low noise with JFET speed (https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/op285.pdf).
Rev. C history: General Description/Pin Connection, Supply Current, Absolute Maximum Ratings (https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/op285.pdf).
RadioLocman copy labelled Revision C, with PDIP outline (https://www.radiolocman.com/datasheet/pdf.html?di=121465&p=14).

PDN 17_0038 covers OP285GS and reels, replacement OP285GSZ; Rev. -, B, C exist (https://www.analog.com/media/en/PCN/ADI_PDN_17_0038_Rev_C_Form.pdf, https://www.mouser.com/PCN/ADI_ADI_PDN_17_0038_Rev_B_Form.pdf, https://mm.digikey.com/Volume0/opasdata/d220001/medias/docus/2206/PDN_17_0038_Rev-.pdf).
OP285GP reported obsolete since April 2002; broker source, medium confidence (https://www.worldwayelec.com/pro/analog-devices/op285gp/5048499).
OP275 is also 9 MHz, same GBW as OP285 (https://uk.rs-online.com/web/p/op-amps/1832628).
refuted_claims: OP285 as 'faster sibling of the OP275' is refuted: both are 9 MHz / 22 V/µs (https://uk.rs-online.com/web/p/op-amps/1832628). Its distinction is the 250 µV trimmed offset.
corrections: OP285 is the precision (trimmed-offset) sibling of the OP275, not a faster one; 'separate die' claim moved to open questions.
